subject: Cognitive Science
title: Circle of Competence
description: A quick, practical guide to Circle of Competence.

hook.text: Warren Buffett avoids tech stocks. Not because they're bad—but because they're outside what he truly knows.

buildup.text: Your circle of competence is the domain where you have real, earned knowledge—not just opinions.

discovery.text: Inside the circle, you can judge risk and spot patterns. Outside, you're guessing but may not know it.

twist.text: The edge of your circle is the danger zone. You know enough to be confident but not enough to be right.

climax.text: Great decision-makers know where their circle ends and either learn more or defer to others.

punchline.text: Know what you know. Know what you don't.

quiz.question: What is the circle of competence?
options: The domain where you have genuine expertise

details.summary: Your circle of competence is the area where you have genuine, tested knowledge through experience. Knowing the boundary of what you truly understand versus what you only think you understand prevents costly mistakes. Staying inside your circle or expanding it deliberately is key.
details.whyItMatters: Most errors come from operating outside your circle of competence without realizing it. Honest self-assessment of what you know is a rare and valuable skill.
takeaways: Know the boundary between real knowledge and assumed knowledge
Operating outside your circle invites costly errors
Expand your circle deliberately through experience, not just reading

faq.question: How do you find the edge of your circle?
faq.answer: Test yourself with real decisions and track results honestly. If you cannot explain something simply, you are probably outside your circle. Seek feedback from genuine experts. The Dunning-Kruger effect means beginners overestimate their competence, so external checks matter.

faq.question: Should you ever act outside your competence circle?
faq.answer: Sometimes you must, but do so with extra caution. Seek expert advice, use checklists, and make smaller bets. Acknowledge your uncertainty explicitly. The danger is not acting outside your circle but doing so while believing you are inside it.
